title: Delta Method
informal: Let $\phi$ be a map between normed spaces that is Fréchet differentiable at $ heta_0$, with continuous linear derivative $\phi^{\prime}$. If the scaling constants satisfy $s_n o\infty$ and $s_n(T_n- heta_0)$ converges weakly to a law $ u$, then — with $T_n$ measurable and $\phi(T_n)$ almost everywhere measurable, so that both sides have laws — the scaled Taylor remainder $s_n igl(\phi(T_n)-\phi( heta_0) igr)-\phi^{\prime} igl(s_n(T_n- heta_0) igr)$ tends to $0$ in probability, and $$s_n igl(\phi(T_n)-\phi( heta_0) igr) ightsquigarrow u\circ(\phi^{\prime})^{-1},$$ the image of $ u$ under the derivative $\phi^{\prime}$.
summary: Weak convergence transports through a differentiable map, with a vanishing first-order Taylor remainder.
leanSignature:
theorem delta_method
    {E F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
      [SecondCountableTopology E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F]
      [SecondCountableTopology F] [Nonempty F]
    {P : ∀ k, Measure (Ω k)} [∀ k, IsProbabilityMeasure (P k)]
    {T : ∀ k, Ω k → E} (hT_meas : ∀ k, Measurable (T k))
    {φ : E → F} {φ' : E →L[ℝ] F} {θ₀ : E}
    (hφ : HasFDerivAt φ φ' θ₀)
    (hφT_meas : ∀ k, AEMeasurable (fun ω => φ (T k ω)) (P k))
    {sqn : ℕ → ℝ} (h_sqn : Tendsto sqn atTop atTop)
    {ν : Measure E} [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (h_wc : WeakConverges (fun k => (P k).map (fun ω => sqn k • (T k ω - θ₀))) ν) :
    WeakConverges (fun k => (P k).map (fun ω => sqn k • (φ (T k ω) - φ θ₀))) (ν.map φ')
      ∧ TendstoInProbZero P
          (fun k ω => sqn k • (φ (T k ω) - φ θ₀ - φ' (T k ω - θ₀)))
formalizationNotes: Consistency and stochastic boundedness are derived internally from weak convergence; they are not hypotheses. The conclusion includes both weak convergence and the theorem's moreover remainder clause.

hypotheses.label: Fréchet differentiability
hypotheses.note: φ is Fréchet differentiable at θ₀, with continuous linear derivative φ'.

hypotheses.label: measurability
hypotheses.note: T_n is measurable and φ(T_n) is almost everywhere measurable, so both statistics have well-defined laws.

hypotheses.label: diverging scale
hypotheses.note: The scaling constants s_n tend to +∞.

hypotheses.label: weak limit of the input
hypotheses.note: The rescaled centred statistic s_n(T_n − θ₀) converges weakly to the law ν.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The delta method's systematic use in asymptotic statistics goes back to H. Cramér, *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*, Princeton University Press, 1946, where limit laws of smooth transformations of asymptotically normal statistics are derived by Taylor expansion ("propagation of error"). Van der Vaart's Theorem 3.1 is the modern formulation: Fréchet differentiability at the centering point transfers the weak limit of the rescaled statistic through $\phi$ in arbitrary normed spaces, with an $o_P$ Taylor remainder; the formalization states both the transferred weak limit and the vanishing remainder.

title: Method-of-Moments Normality
informal: Let $X_1,X_2,\dots$ be independent and identically distributed with law $P$, let $f$ be a measurable $\mathbb R^d$-valued moment function that is square-integrable under $P$, and let the moment map $e$ have a strict derivative $e^{\prime}_{\theta_0}$ at $\theta_0$ that is a continuous linear isomorphism, with $e(\theta_0)=\int f\,dP$. Then there are measurable estimators $\hat\theta_n$ solving the moment equation $e(\hat\theta_n)=\mathbb P_nf:=n^{-1}\sum_{i\le n}f(X_i)$ with probability tending to one, and they satisfy the linear representation $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=(e^{\prime}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\Bigl(\sqrt n\bigl(\mathbb P_nf-\textstyle\int f\,dP\bigr)\Bigr)+o_P(1),$$ so that $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)\rightsquigarrow N\bigl(0,\,(e^{\prime}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\operatorname{Cov}_P(f)\,\bigl((e^{\prime}_{\theta_0})^{-1}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)$.
summary: A measurable solution of the moment equation exists asymptotically and is asymptotically linear and Gaussian.
leanSignature:
theorem method_of_moments_normality {d : ℕ}
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    {f : Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)} (hf_meas : Measurable f) (hf_L2 : MemLp f 2 P)
    {e : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    {e' : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    {θ₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    (he : HasStrictFDerivAt e (e' : _ →L[ℝ] _) θ₀)
    (hμ : e θ₀ = ∫ x, f x ∂P)
    {Ξ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] {μ : Measure Ξ} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ξ → Ω} (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hX_indep : iIndepFun X μ)
    (hX_id : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hX_law : μ.map (X 0) = P) :
    ∃ θhat : ℕ → Ξ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (∀ n, Measurable (θhat n)) ∧
      Tendsto (fun n => μ.real {ξ | e (θhat n ξ) = empiricalMoment f n X ξ}) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      TendstoInProbZero (fun _ : ℕ => μ)
        (fun n ξ => Real.sqrt n • (θhat n ξ - θ₀)
          - (↑e'.symm : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
              (Real.sqrt n • (empiricalMoment f n X ξ - ∫ x, f x ∂P))) ∧
      WeakConverges (fun n => μ.map (fun ξ => Real.sqrt n • (θhat n ξ - θ₀)))
        (multivariateGaussian 0 (momentLimitCov P f e'))
formalizationNotes: Estimator existence and measurability are conclusions. Consistency and tightness are derived from the empirical-moment CLT.

hypotheses.label: square-integrable moments
hypotheses.note: f is measurable and square-integrable under P.

hypotheses.label: invertible derivative
hypotheses.note: e has a strict derivative at θ₀ which is a continuous linear isomorphism, hence invertible.

hypotheses.label: moment identity
hypotheses.note: The moment map matches the true moment: e(θ₀) = ∫ f dP.

hypotheses.label: i.i.d. sample from P
hypotheses.note: The observations are independent, identically distributed, with marginal law P.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The method of moments goes back to K. Pearson, "Contributions to the mathematical theory of evolution," *Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A* **185** (1894), 71–110, where mixture parameters were fitted by matching empirical moments. Asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators is the classical combination of the central limit theorem for empirical moments with the delta method for the inverse moment map (Cramér 1946); van der Vaart's Theorem 4.1 states local existence, consistency, and normality under an invertible derivative of the moment map.

title: M-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $M_n$ be random criterion functions on a metric parameter set $\Theta$ and $M$ a deterministic limit criterion. If a measurable envelope $U_n$ dominates the uniform error, $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}|M_n(\theta)-M(\theta)|\le U_n$, and $U_n\to_P0$; if $\theta_0$ is a well-separated maximum of $M$, i.e. for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\eta>0$ with $M(\theta)\le M(\theta_0)-\eta$ whenever $d(\theta,\theta_0)\ge\varepsilon$; and if $\hat\theta_n$ almost maximizes $M_n$, in the sense that $M_n(\hat\theta_n)\ge M_n(\theta_0)-R_n$ for a slack $R_n\to_P0$; then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Uniform criterion convergence plus a separated population maximum makes every near-maximizer consistent.
leanSignature:
theorem mEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Type*} [MetricSpace Θ]
    {Mn : ℕ → Ω → Θ → ℝ} {M : Θ → ℝ} {θ₀ : Θ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → Θ}
    {U R : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hU_dom : ∀ n ω θ, |Mn n ω θ - M θ| ≤ U n ω)
    (hU_conv : TendstoInMeasure P U atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)))
    (hsep : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ η > (0 : ℝ), ∀ θ, ε ≤ dist θ θ₀ → M θ ≤ M θ₀ - η)
    (hnear : ∀ n ω, Mn n ω θ₀ - R n ω ≤ Mn n ω (θhat n ω))
    (hR_conv : TendstoInMeasure P R atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ dist (θhat n ω) θ₀}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: The envelope encodes the uniform error without requiring measurability of a supremum. Neither estimator measurability nor a probability-measure instance is required.

hypotheses.label: uniform convergence
hypotheses.note: A measurable envelope dominates the uniform criterion error sup_θ |M_n(θ) − M(θ)| and tends to zero in probability.

hypotheses.label: separated maximum
hypotheses.note: For every ε > 0 there is η > 0 with M(θ) ≤ M(θ₀) − η whenever θ is at distance at least ε from θ₀.

hypotheses.label: near maximization
hypotheses.note: The maximizing slack R_n in M_n(θ̂_n) ≥ M_n(θ₀) − R_n tends to zero in probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The argmax-plus-uniform-convergence route to consistency originates with A. Wald, "Note on the consistency of the maximum likelihood estimate," *The Annals of Mathematical Statistics* **20** (1949), 595–601, for maximum likelihood; P. J. Huber, "The behavior of maximum likelihood estimates under nonstandard conditions," *Fifth Berkeley Symposium* (1967), extended it to general M-estimators. The well-separated-maximum formulation used here is van der Vaart's Theorem 5.7, following the empirical-process treatment of van der Vaart and Wellner (1996).

title: Z-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $\Psi_n$ be random maps from a metric parameter set $\Theta$ into a normed space and $\Psi$ a deterministic limit. If a measurable envelope $U_n$ dominates the uniform error, $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\|\Psi_n(\theta)-\Psi(\theta)\|\le U_n$, and $U_n\to_P0$; if $\Psi(\theta_0)=0$ and the zero is separated, i.e. for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\eta>0$ with $\|\Psi(\theta)\|\ge\eta$ whenever $d(\theta,\theta_0)\ge\varepsilon$; and if $\|\Psi_n(\hat\theta_n)\|\to_P0$; then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Uniform estimating-equation convergence and zero separation imply consistency of near-roots.
leanSignature:
theorem zEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Type*} [MetricSpace Θ]
    {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    {Ψn : ℕ → Ω → Θ → F} {Ψ : Θ → F} {θ₀ : Θ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → Θ}
    {U : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hU_dom : ∀ n ω θ, ‖Ψn n ω θ - Ψ θ‖ ≤ U n ω)
    (hU_conv : TendstoInMeasure P U atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)))
    (hΨ0 : Ψ θ₀ = 0)
    (hsep : ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ η > (0 : ℝ), ∀ θ, ε ≤ dist θ θ₀ → η ≤ ‖Ψ θ‖)
    (hnear : TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => ‖Ψn n ω (θhat n ω)‖) atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ dist (θhat n ω) θ₀}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: Reduced internally to M-estimator consistency with criterion −‖Ψ‖; no estimator measurability is assumed.

hypotheses.label: uniform convergence
hypotheses.note: A measurable envelope dominates sup_θ ‖Ψ_n(θ) − Ψ(θ)‖ and tends to zero in probability.

hypotheses.label: identified separated zero
hypotheses.note: Ψ vanishes at θ₀, and for every ε > 0 the norm ‖Ψ(θ)‖ stays above a positive constant at distance at least ε from θ₀.

hypotheses.label: approximate root
hypotheses.note: The estimating function evaluated at the estimator, ‖Ψ_n(θ̂_n)‖, tends to zero in probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Estimators defined by vanishing criterion functions descend from the classical analysis of likelihood equations (Cramér 1946) and P. J. Huber's M-estimators of location (1964) and their nonstandard-conditions theory (1967). Van der Vaart's Theorem 5.9 isolates the well-separated-zero condition under uniform convergence of the criterion; the Lean statement phrases the uniform convergence through a measurable envelope, replacing the book's outer probability of a possibly non-measurable supremum.

title: Monotone One-Dimensional Z-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$ be order-connected: whenever it contains two points it contains the whole interval between them, and let $\Psi_n:\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be random functions that are nondecreasing on $\Theta$. Assume $\Psi_n(\theta)\to_P\Psi(\theta)$ for each fixed $\theta\in\Theta$, and the limit changes sign strictly at $\theta_0$: $\Psi(\theta)<0$ for $\theta<\theta_0$ and $\Psi(\theta)>0$ for $\theta>\theta_0$. If the estimators take values in $\Theta$ and $\Psi_n(\hat\theta_n)\to_P0$, then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Pointwise convergence and monotonicity turn a strict sign change into consistency of approximate roots.
leanSignature:
theorem oneDim_monotone_zEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Set ℝ} (hΘ : Θ.OrdConnected)
    {Ψn : ℕ → Ω → ℝ → ℝ} {Ψ : ℝ → ℝ} {θ₀ : ℝ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hθ₀ : θ₀ ∈ Θ)
    (hθhat : ∀ n ω, θhat n ω ∈ Θ)
    (hmono : ∀ n ω, MonotoneOn (Ψn n ω) Θ)
    (hptwise : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => Ψn n ω θ) atTop (fun _ => Ψ θ))
    (hnear : TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => Ψn n ω (θhat n ω)) atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)))
    (hsign_lt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ < θ₀ → Ψ θ < 0)
    (hsign_gt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ₀ < θ → 0 < Ψ θ) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ |θhat n ω - θ₀|}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: Works for a general measure and needs no estimator measurability. Order-connectedness handles boundary cases without an interior-point assumption.

hypotheses.label: order-connected domain
hypotheses.note: Θ contains the whole interval between any two of its points.

hypotheses.label: monotonicity
hypotheses.note: Each random estimating function is nondecreasing on Θ.

hypotheses.label: pointwise limit with strict sign change
hypotheses.note: Ψ_n(θ) → Ψ(θ) in probability for each fixed θ, and Ψ is strictly negative left of θ₀ and strictly positive right of θ₀.

hypotheses.label: approximate root
hypotheses.note: The estimating function evaluated at the estimator tends to zero in probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: For monotone criteria the argument is the classical device behind sample quantiles and location M-estimators with monotone influence functions, P. J. Huber, "Robust estimation of a location parameter," *The Annals of Mathematical Statistics* **35** (1964), 73–101: monotonicity converts pointwise convergence at two flanking points into consistency, with no uniformity over the parameter needed. Van der Vaart's Lemma 5.10 records both the monotone and the continuous unique-zero cases; this entry formalizes the monotone case.

title: Continuous One-Dimensional Z-Estimator Consistency
informal: Let $\Psi_n:\Theta\to\mathbb R$ be random functions on $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R$, where $\Theta$ is a neighbourhood of $\theta_0$. Assume each $\Psi_n$ is continuous on $\Theta$ and has $\hat\theta_n$ as its only zero there: $\Psi_n(\theta)=0$ with $\theta\in\Theta$ forces $\theta=\hat\theta_n$, and $\Psi_n(\theta)\to_P\Psi(\theta)$ for each fixed $\theta\in\Theta$, with $\Psi(\theta)<0$ for $\theta<\theta_0$ and $\Psi(\theta)>0$ for $\theta>\theta_0$. Then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: Continuity, uniqueness, pointwise convergence, and a strict sign change imply consistency of the one-dimensional root.
leanSignature:
theorem oneDim_continuous_zEstimator_consistent
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {Θ : Set ℝ}
    {Ψn : ℕ → Ω → ℝ → ℝ} {Ψ : ℝ → ℝ} {θ₀ : ℝ} {θhat : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
    (hθ₀_int : Θ ∈ 𝓝 θ₀)
    (hcont : ∀ n ω, ContinuousOn (Ψn n ω) Θ)
    (hunique : ∀ n ω θ, θ ∈ Θ → Ψn n ω θ = 0 → θ = θhat n ω)
    (hptwise : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, TendstoInMeasure P (fun n ω => Ψn n ω θ) atTop (fun _ => Ψ θ))
    (hsign_lt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ < θ₀ → Ψ θ < 0)
    (hsign_gt : ∀ θ ∈ Θ, θ₀ < θ → 0 < Ψ θ) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), Tendsto (fun n => P {ω | ε ≤ |θhat n ω - θ₀|}) atTop (𝓝 0)
formalizationNotes: Interiority is explicit and necessary for this continuous route. The theorem does not separately assume that $\hat\theta_n$ lies in Θ or is measurable.

hypotheses.label: interior truth
hypotheses.note: Θ is a neighbourhood of θ₀.

hypotheses.label: continuity and unique zero
hypotheses.note: Each Ψ_n is continuous on Θ and every zero of Ψ_n in Θ equals the estimator θ̂_n.

hypotheses.label: pointwise limit with strict sign change
hypotheses.note: Ψ_n(θ) → Ψ(θ) in probability for each fixed θ, and Ψ is strictly negative left of θ₀ and strictly positive right of θ₀.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Producing a consistent zero of a continuous one-dimensional criterion from a sign change (an intermediate-value argument) is the classical device behind consistent roots of likelihood equations, H. Cramér, *Mathematical Methods of Statistics*, 1946. Van der Vaart's Lemma 5.10 records both the monotone and the continuous unique-zero cases; this entry formalizes the continuous case, where uniqueness of the zero pins the estimator.

title: Z-Estimator Asymptotic Normality
informal: Let $\psi_\theta=(\psi_{\theta,1},\dots,\psi_{\theta,k})$ be measurable estimating functions on $\mathbb R^k$ with a local Lipschitz property in $L^2(P)$: $|\psi_{\theta_1,j}(x)-\psi_{\theta_2,j}(x)|\le m(x)\,\|\theta_1-\theta_2\|$ for all $\theta_1,\theta_2$ in a fixed ball around $\theta_0$, with $m$ square-integrable under $P$. Assume $\int\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP=0$ and $\psi_{\theta_0}\in L^2(P)$, and that $\theta\mapsto\int\psi_\theta\,dP$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ with nonsingular derivative matrix $V$. If the observations are i.i.d. $P$, $\hat\theta_n$ is measurable and consistent for $\theta_0$, and $\hat\theta_n$ solves the estimating equation to order $o_P(n^{-1/2})$, i.e. $\sqrt n\,\mathbb P_n\psi_{\hat\theta_n,j}\to0$ in outer probability uniformly in the coordinate $j$, then $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)\rightsquigarrow N\bigl(0,\ V^{-1}\,P\psi_{\theta_0}\psi_{\theta_0}^{\mathsf T}\,(V^{-1})^{\mathsf T}\bigr).$$
summary: A consistent approximate Z-root is asymptotically Gaussian under local Lipschitz, differentiability, and L² conditions.
leanSignature:
theorem zEstimator_asymptotic_normality
    {k : ℕ} {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → Fin k → (Ω → ℝ))
    (θ₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (V : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ)
    (hV : IsUnit V.det) (δcls : ℝ) (hδcls : 0 < δcls)
    (m : Ω → ℝ) (hm : MemLp m 2 P) (hm_meas : Measurable m)
    (hLip : ∀ θ₁ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), ‖θ₁ - θ₀‖ < δcls →
      ∀ θ₂ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), ‖θ₂ - θ₀‖ < δcls →
      ∀ (j : Fin k) (x : Ω), |ψ θ₁ j x - ψ θ₂ j x| ≤ m x * ‖θ₁ - θ₂‖)
    (hψ_meas : ∀ (θ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (j : Fin k), Measurable (ψ θ j))
    (hPθ₀_zero : ∀ h, ∫ x, ψ θ₀ h x ∂P = 0)
    (hfrechet : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ θ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k),
        0 < ‖θ - θ₀‖ → ‖θ - θ₀‖ < δ →
        (⨆ h, ENNReal.ofReal
            |∫ x, ψ θ h x ∂P - ∫ x, ψ θ₀ h x ∂P - Vlin V (θ - θ₀) h|)
          ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (ε * ‖θ - θ₀‖))
    (hψ_L2 : MemLp (psiVec ψ θ₀) 2 P)
    (θ_hat : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
    {Ξ : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (μ : Measure Ξ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X : ℕ → Ξ → Ω) (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hX_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
    (hX_id : ∀ i, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hX_law : μ.map (X 0) = P)
    (hθhat_meas' : ∀ n, Measurable
      (fun ξ : Ξ => θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ)))
    (h_consist : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → Tendsto (fun n =>
      μ {ξ | ε < ‖θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) - θ₀‖}) atTop (𝓝 0))
    (h_est_eq : TendstoZeroInOuterProbSup μ (fun n ξ h =>
      Real.sqrt n * empiricalAvg (ψ (θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ)) h)
        n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ))) :
    WeakConverges
      (fun n => μ.map (fun ξ =>
        Real.sqrt n • (θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) - θ₀)))
      (multivariateGaussian 0 (V⁻¹ * psiCov P ψ θ₀ * (V⁻¹)ᵀ))
formalizationNotes: The parametric Donsker and tightness inputs are derived internally. Estimator measurability is explicitly present as `hθhat_meas'`.

hypotheses.label: local L² Lipschitz class
hypotheses.note: Near θ₀ the estimating functions are Lipschitz in θ with a square-P-integrable envelope m.

hypotheses.label: nonsingular derivative
hypotheses.note: θ ↦ ∫ ψ_θ dP is Fréchet differentiable at θ₀ with nonsingular derivative matrix V.

hypotheses.label: measurable consistent estimator
hypotheses.note: The estimator is measurable in the sample and converges to θ₀ in probability.

hypotheses.label: approximate estimating equation
hypotheses.note: The estimating equation at the estimator is of order o_P(n^(−1/2)), uniformly over coordinates in outer probability.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Asymptotic normality of Z-estimators under weak smoothness goes back to P. J. Huber (1967), who replaced pointwise differentiability of the criterion by differentiability of its expectation plus a stochastic remainder condition. The modern proof via empirical-process theory — Donsker classes and asymptotic equicontinuity of the empirical process indexed by the criterion functions — was introduced by D. Pollard, "New ways to prove central limit theorems," *Econometric Theory* **1** (1985), 295–313, and systematized in van der Vaart and Wellner (1996). Van der Vaart's Theorem 5.21 is the Lipschitz-class master theorem of this kind.

title: M-Estimator Asymptotic Normality
informal: Let $m_\theta$ be measurable criterion functions on $\mathbb R^d$ with a local $L^2$ Lipschitz property, $|m_{\theta_1}(x)-m_{\theta_2}(x)|\le \dot m_{\mathrm{env}}(x)\|\theta_1-\theta_2\|$ on a ball around $\theta_0$ with $\dot m_{\mathrm{env}}$ square-$P$-integrable, and an almost sure derivative $\dot m_{\theta_0}$ at $\theta_0$. Assume the population criterion has the quadratic expansion $\int(m_\theta-m_{\theta_0})\,dP=\tfrac12(\theta-\theta_0)^{\mathsf T}V(\theta-\theta_0)+o(\|\theta-\theta_0\|^2)$ with $V$ symmetric and uniformly negative definite: $x^{\mathsf T}Vx\le-c\|x\|^2$ for some $c>0$. title: Z-Estimator Representation with Estimated Nuisance
informal: Let $\psi_{\theta,\eta}$ be measurable estimating functions depending on the parameter $\theta\in\mathbb R^k$ and a nuisance $\eta$ in a metric space, with $\int\psi_{\theta_0,\eta_0}\,dP=0$. Assume the local class $\{\psi_{\theta,\eta}:\|\theta-\theta_0\|<\delta,\ d(\eta,\eta_0)<\delta\}$ is $P$-Donsker and $L^2(P)$-continuous at $(\theta_0,\eta_0)$, i.e. $\int(\psi_{\theta,\eta}-\psi_{\theta_0,\eta_0})^2\,dP\to0$ as $(\theta,\eta)\to(\theta_0,\eta_0)$, and $\theta\mapsto\int\psi_{\theta,\eta}\,dP$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ uniformly over $\eta$ near $\eta_0$, with derivative matrix $V_\eta$ continuous at $\eta_0$ and $V_{\eta_0}$ nonsingular. If the observations are i.i.d. $P$, $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$ and $\hat\eta_n\to_P\eta_0$, and $\sqrt n\,\mathbb P_n\psi_{\hat\theta_n,\hat\eta_n}\to0$ in outer probability, then $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=-V_{\eta_0}^{-1}\Bigl(\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\le n}\psi_{\theta_0,\eta_0}(X_i)+\sqrt n\int\psi_{\theta_0,\hat\eta_n}\,dP\Bigr)+o_P(1),$$ the remainder being $o_P(1)$ after division by $1+\sqrt n\,\bigl\|\int\psi_{\theta_0,\hat\eta_n}\,dP\bigr\|$. The second term inside the brackets is the drift contributed by estimating the nuisance; it vanishes when $\eta_0$ is known.
summary: A Z-estimator with an estimated nuisance has the weighted linear representation including the nuisance drift term.

title: MLE Consistency from KL Identifiability
citation: van der Vaart (1998), Thm 5.7 route + Lem 5.35
informal: Let $\{p_\theta\}$ be a family of genuine probability densities relative to $\mu$ whose parametrization is identifiable at $\theta_0$: if $p_\theta\,d\mu=p_{\theta_0}\,d\mu$ then $\theta=\theta_0$. Write $M(\theta)=\int\log\frac{p_\theta+p_{\theta_0}}{2p_{\theta_0}}\,dP_{\theta_0}$ for the stabilized population criterion, a bounded-above surrogate for the negative Kullback–Leibler divergence which identifiability makes uniquely maximal at $\theta_0$. Assume $M$ is upper semicontinuous and some superlevel set $\{\theta:M(\theta)\ge c\}$ with $c. If a measurable envelope $U_n$ dominates the uniform criterion error $\sup_\theta\bigl|\mathbb P_n\log\frac{p_\theta+p_{\theta_0}}{2p_{\theta_0}}-M(\theta)\bigr|$ and $U_n\to_P0$, and $\hat\theta_n$ maximizes the likelihood $\prod_{i\le n}p_\theta(X_i)$ exactly, then $\hat\theta_n\to_P\theta_0$.
summary: KL identifiability, compact separation, uniform convergence, and exact likelihood maximization imply MLE consistency.

title: Maximum-Likelihood Asymptotic Normality
informal: Let $\{p_\theta\}$ be a family of probability densities relative to $\mu$ that is identifiable at $\theta_0$ and differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell_{\theta_0}$. title: Classical Z-Estimator Normality
informal: Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k$ be open with $\theta_0\in\Theta$, and let $\psi_\theta$ be measurable estimating functions such that $\theta\mapsto\psi_\theta(x)$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\Theta$, with second derivatives dominated on a closed ball around $\theta_0$ by one fixed $P$-integrable function $\ddot\psi$. Assume $\int\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP=0$, $\psi_{\theta_0}\in L^2(P)$, the derivative $\dot\psi_{\theta_0}$ is $P$-integrable, and $V=\int\dot\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP$ is nonsingular. If the data are i.i.d. $P$, $\hat\theta_n$ is measurable and consistent for $\theta_0$, and the event $\{\mathbb P_n\psi_{\hat\theta_n}=0\}$ that $\hat\theta_n$ is an exact root has inner probability tending to one, then $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=-V^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\le n}\psi_{\theta_0}(X_i)+o_P(1)\rightsquigarrow N\bigl(0,\ V^{-1}P\psi_{\theta_0}\psi_{\theta_0}^{\mathsf T}(V^{-1})^{\mathsf T}\bigr).$$
summary: A measurable consistent classical Z-root is asymptotically linear and Gaussian under smoothness and domination.

theorem classical_zEstimator_normality
    {k : ℕ} {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (Θ : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))) (hΘ_open : IsOpen Θ)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → Fin k → Ω → ℝ)
    (θ₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (hθ₀ : θ₀ ∈ Θ)
    (hψ_meas : ∀ θ j, Measurable (ψ θ j))
    (hC2 : ∀ (j : Fin k) (x : Ω), ContDiffOn ℝ 2 (fun θ => ψ θ j x) Θ)
    (hPθ₀_zero : ∀ j, ∫ x, ψ θ₀ j x ∂P = 0)
    (hψ_L2 : MemLp (psiVec ψ θ₀) 2 P)
    (hVint : ∀ j i, Integrable (fun x => psiDot ψ θ₀ x j i) P)
    (hV : IsUnit (Vmat P ψ θ₀).det)
    (ψddot : Ω → ℝ) (hψddot_meas : Measurable ψddot) (hψddot_int : Integrable ψddot P)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hball : Metric.closedBall θ₀ ρ ⊆ Θ)
    (hdom : ∀ θ ∈ Metric.closedBall θ₀ ρ, ∀ (j : Fin k) (x : Ω),
      ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 (fun θ' => ψ θ' j x) θ‖ ≤ ψddot x)
    (θ_hat : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
    {Ξ : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ξ] (μ : Measure Ξ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (X : ℕ → Ξ → Ω) (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hX_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
    (hX_id : ∀ i, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ)
    (hX_law : μ.map (X 0) = P)
    (hθhat_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (fun ξ : Ξ => θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ)))
    (hroot : TendstoInnerProbOne μ (fun n => {ξ | ∀ j,
      empiricalAvg (ψ (θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ)) j) n
        (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) = 0}))
    (hcons : TendstoInProbZero (fun _ : ℕ => μ)
      (fun n ξ => θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) - θ₀)) :
    TendstoInProbZero (fun _ : ℕ => μ) (fun n ξ =>
        Real.sqrt n • (θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) - θ₀)
          + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin k) (Vmat P ψ θ₀)⁻¹
              (empiricalProcessVec P ψ θ₀ n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ)))
    ∧ WeakConverges
        (fun n => μ.map (fun ξ => Real.sqrt n • (θ_hat n (fun i : Fin n => X i.val ξ) - θ₀)))
        (multivariateGaussian 0 ((Vmat P ψ θ₀)⁻¹ * psiCov P ψ θ₀ * ((Vmat P ψ θ₀)⁻¹)ᵀ))
formalizationNotes: This ordinary weak-convergence theorem explicitly includes estimator measurability `hθhat_meas`. Root validity is allowed on events whose inner probability tends to one.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The twice-continuously-differentiable, dominated-second-derivative conditions are the classical Cramér conditions for the likelihood equations: H. Van der Vaart's Theorem 5.41 restates the argument for general estimating equations: a second-order Taylor expansion of the empirical criterion around $\theta_0$, the law of large numbers for the derivative matrices, and the central limit theorem for the score term.

title: Classical Z-Root Existence and Consistency
informal: Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k$ be open with $\theta_0\in\Theta$, and let $\psi_\theta$ be measurable estimating functions such that $\theta\mapsto\psi_\theta(x)$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\Theta$, with second derivatives dominated on a closed ball around $\theta_0$ by one fixed $P$-integrable function. Assume $\int\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP=0$, $\psi_{\theta_0}\in L^2(P)$, the derivative $\dot\psi_{\theta_0}$ is $P$-integrable, and $V=\int\dot\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP$ is nonsingular, and that $X_1,X_2,\dots$ are measurable, independent and identically distributed with law $P$. Then the event that the empirical estimating equation $\mathbb P_n\psi_\theta=0$ has at least one solution $\theta\in\Theta$ carries inner probability tending to one, and one may choose such roots $\hat\theta_n$ forming a sequence consistent for $\theta_0$.
summary: Classical smooth estimating equations have a consistent root with inner probability tending to one.

    (ψddot : Ω → ℝ) (hψddot_meas : Measurable ψddot) (hψddot_int : Integrable ψddot P)

title: Existence of a Normal Classical Z-Root
informal: Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^k$ be open with $\theta_0\in\Theta$, and let $\psi_\theta$ be measurable estimating functions such that $\theta\mapsto\psi_\theta(x)$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\Theta$, with second derivatives dominated near $\theta_0$ by one fixed $P$-integrable function. Assume $\int\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP=0$, $\psi_{\theta_0}\in L^2(P)$, the derivative $\dot\psi_{\theta_0}$ is $P$-integrable, and $V=\int\dot\psi_{\theta_0}\,dP$ is nonsingular, and that the observations are measurable, independent and identically distributed with law $P$. Then roots of $\mathbb P_n\psi_\theta=0$ in $\Theta$ exist with inner probability tending to one, and one may select a consistent root sequence $\hat\theta_n$ satisfying $$\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)=-V^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\le n}\psi_{\theta_0}(X_i)+o_P(1)$$ together with the outer weak convergence $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n-\theta_0)\rightsquigarrow N\bigl(0,V^{-1}P\psi_{\theta_0}\psi_{\theta_0}^{\mathsf T}(V^{-1})^{\mathsf T}\bigr)$ — outer, because the selected roots need not be measurable.
summary: A consistent classical Z-root exists asymptotically and enjoys the linear representation and outer Gaussian limit without a measurable selection.

title: Differentiability in Quadratic Mean
informal: A parametric model $M$ is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta$ with score $\ell$ relative to the dominating measure $\mu$ if the Hellinger residual lies in $L^2(\mu)$ for $h$ near $0$ and the square-root densities admit the $L^2(\mu)$ expansion $$\int\Big(\sqrt{p_{\theta+h}}-\sqrt{p_\theta}-\tfrac12\langle h,\ell\rangle\sqrt{p_\theta}\Big)^2\,d\mu = o(\|h\|^2)$$ as $h\to0$.
summary: A parametric model is differentiable in quadratic mean at theta with score ell when the Hellinger residual of the square-root densities is o-of-norm-h-squared in L2.
leanSignature:
structure DifferentiableQuadraticMean
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 Θ) (μ : Measure 𝓧) (θ : Θ)
    (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ) : Prop where
  mem : ∀ᶠ h in 𝓝 (0 : Θ),
    MemLp (fun x => M.sqrtDensity (θ + h) x - M.sqrtDensity θ x
                    - (1/2 : ℝ) * ⟪h, ℓ x⟫ * M.sqrtDensity θ x) 2 μ
  isLittleO :
    (fun h : Θ =>
      ∫ x, (M.sqrtDensity (θ + h) x
            - M.sqrtDensity θ x
            - (1/2 : ℝ) * ⟪h, ℓ x⟫ * M.sqrtDensity θ x) ^ 2 ∂μ)
    =o[𝓝 (0 : Θ)] (fun h : Θ => ‖h‖ ^ 2)
formalizationNotes: The structure adds the field `mem` (residual eventually in L2(mu)) which is implicit in the Lebesgue-integral formulation but must be stated explicitly because Lean's Bochner integral assigns value 0 to non-integrable functions; the explicit L2-membership conjunct makes the formal statement equivalent to the Lebesgue-integral version.

hypotheses.label: square-integrable residual
hypotheses.note: The Hellinger residual √p_{θ+h} − √p_θ − ½⟨h, ℓ⟩√p_θ is square-integrable against μ for every h in a neighbourhood of 0, so the displayed integral is finite.

hypotheses.label: o(‖h‖²) rate
hypotheses.note: The integrated squared Hellinger residual is of smaller order than ‖h‖² as h → 0.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Differentiability in quadratic mean originates with L. Le Cam, "On the assumptions used to prove asymptotic normality of maximum likelihood estimates," *The Annals of Mathematical Statistics* **41** (1970), no. 3, 802–828, who introduced this $L^2$/Hellinger differentiability of the root density as the minimal regularity replacing the classical pointwise smoothness-and-domination conditions, and used it to establish local asymptotic normality and asymptotic normality of the MLE. Van der Vaart's §7.2 (Eq. 7.1) and §25.3 (Lemma 25.14) restate this notion.

title: Quadratic-Mean-Differentiable Path
informal: A dominated quadratic-mean-differentiable path at a probability measure $P$ is a curve $t\mapsto Q_t$ of probability measures with $Q_0=P$, each dominated by a fixed $\sigma$-finite measure $\mu$, together with a score $g\in L^2_0(P)$ (mean zero, square-integrable) such that $$\big\|\sqrt{p_t}-\sqrt{p_0}-\tfrac{t}{2}\,g\,\sqrt{p_0}\big\|_{L^2(\mu)}\big/|t|\to0$$ as $t\to0$, where the densities $p_t$ are Radon–Nikodym derivatives of $Q_t$ with respect to $\mu$.
summary: A curve of probability measures through P, dominated by a fixed measure, with an L2-zero-mean score whose half is the L2 derivative of the square-root density.
leanSignature:
structure QMDPath (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] where
  curve : ℝ → Measure Ω
  curve_at_zero : curve 0 = P
  curve_isProbability : ∀ t, IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t)
  dominating : Measure Ω
  curve_absContinuous : ∀ t, curve t ≪ dominating
  dominating_sigmaFinite : SigmaFinite dominating
  score : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)
  qmd_limit :
    Tendsto
      (fun t : ℝ =>
        eLpNorm (fun ω : Ω =>
          Real.sqrt ((curve t).rnDeriv dominating ω).toReal
            - Real.sqrt ((curve 0).rnDeriv dominating ω).toReal
            - (t / 2) * (score : Ω → ℝ) ω
                * Real.sqrt ((curve 0).rnDeriv dominating ω).toReal)
          2 dominating / ENNReal.ofReal |t|)
      (𝓝[≠] 0) (𝓝 (0 : ℝ≥0∞))
formalizationNotes: Formalizes the dominated specialisation: a fixed sigma-finite dominating measure and densities via Radon–Nikodym derivatives. The score's type ↥(L2ZeroMean P) bakes in mean-zero + square-integrability. The qmd_limit is stated in ℝ≥0∞-quotient form so it genuinely forces the residual into L²(μ) near 0, rather than being vacuously satisfied by the .toReal form.

hypotheses.label: quadratic-mean limit
hypotheses.note: The L²(μ) norm of the square-root-density residual, divided by |t|, tends to 0 as t → 0.

hypotheses.label: passes through P

hypotheses.label: common dominating measure

hypotheses.label: mean-zero square-integrable score

title: Regular Estimator Sequence
informal: An estimator sequence $T_n$ for $\psi(\theta)$ is regular at $\theta_0$ if there exists a limit probability measure $L_\theta$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that for every $h\in\mathbb{R}^k$, $$\sqrt n\,\big(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n)\big)\xrightarrow{P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}} L_\theta,$$ with the limit $L_\theta$ the same for every $h$. The independence of $L_\theta$ from $h$ is the regularity requirement.
summary: An estimator sequence whose rescaled recentred statistic converges weakly to one common h-independent limit law under each local alternative.
leanSignature:
structure RegularEstimatorSequence
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧)
    (θ₀ : AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k)
    (ψ : AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k → AsymptoticRepresentation.𝓨 d)
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → AsymptoticRepresentation.𝓨 d) : Type where
  limitDist : Measure (AsymptoticRepresentation.𝓨 d)
  isProb : IsProbabilityMeasure limitDist
  tendsto : ∀ h : AsymptoticRepresentation.Θ k,
    WeakConverges
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (AsymptoticRepresentation.productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n).map
          (fun x => (Real.sqrt n) •
            (T n x - ψ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h))))
      limitDist
formalizationNotes: `isProb` records the explicit 'probability measure' qualifier on L_θ. Weak convergence uses the project's WeakConverges test-function form. The estimator T is a sequence of measurable maps on the n-fold product space.

hypotheses.label: shift-invariant weak limit
hypotheses.note: For every h, √n(T_n − ψ(θ₀ + h/√n)) converges weakly under the local alternative to the limit law.

hypotheses.label: common limit law
hypotheses.note: One limit distribution L_θ serves for every h; that independence of h is exactly regularity.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The regular-estimator concept and the convolution theorem it feeds originate with J. Hájek, "A characterization of limiting distributions of regular estimates," *Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete* **14** (1970), 323–330, with an independent contemporary treatment by T. Inagaki, "On the limiting distribution of a sequence of estimators with uniformity property," *Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics* **22** (1970), 1–13. The modern local-asymptotic-minimax framing is due to L. Le Cam (*Asymptotic Methods in Statistical Decision Theory*, Springer, 1986); vdV §8.5 follows that synthesis.

title: Bowl-Shaped Loss Function
informal: A loss function $L:E\to[0,\infty]$ is bowl-shaped if it is measurable, symmetric about the origin ($L(-x)=L(x)$), and has convex sublevel sets $\{x : L(x)\le c\}$.
summary: A measurable, origin-symmetric loss with convex sublevel sets; the standing loss assumption for the local asymptotic minimax theorem.
leanSignature:
structure BowlShaped [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
    (L : E → ℝ≥0∞) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable L
  symm : ∀ x, L (-x) = L x
  convex_sublevel : ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, Convex ℝ {x | L x ≤ c}
formalizationNotes: This is bowl-shaped only, not subconvex: the latter is reserved for bowl-shaped with closed sublevel sets (lower semicontinuous), which this structure does not require — there is no lsc/closed-sublevel field. Measurability is kept as an explicit field (implicit in the original) so the structure works for E more general than ℝ^d. Codomain ℝ≥0∞ (the original uses [0,∞)) matches Mathlib's risk framework and is a no-op for finite-valued losses.

hypotheses.label: measurability
hypotheses.note: L is measurable, so its integrals against the candidate limit laws are defined.

hypotheses.label: symmetry
hypotheses.note: L is symmetric about the origin: L(−x) = L(x).

hypotheses.label: convex sublevel sets
hypotheses.note: Every sublevel set {x : L(x) ≤ c} is convex; with symmetry these are convex symmetric sets.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.

title: Gaussian Shift Experiment
informal: The Gaussian shift experiment with covariance $\Sigma$ is the family of laws on $\mathbb R^k$ indexed by a shift $h\in\mathbb R^k$ whose $h$-th member is a Gaussian probability measure with mean $h$, i.e. $\int\langle u,x\rangle\,dN(h,\Sigma)(x)=\langle u,h\rangle$ for every $u$ and covariance $\Sigma$, i.e. $\int\langle u,x-h\rangle\langle w,x-h\rangle\,dN(h,\Sigma)(x)=\langle u,\Sigma w\rangle$ for all $u,w$, where $\Sigma$ is positive definite. In short, the $h$-th member is $N(h,\Sigma)$.
summary: The family h to N(h, Sigma) of Gaussian probability measures with mean h and fixed positive-definite covariance Sigma, the limit experiment of local asymptotic normality.
leanSignature:
structure IsGaussianShift
    (family : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)))
    (cov : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) : Prop where
  posDef : Matrix.PosDef cov
  isProb : ∀ h, IsProbabilityMeasure (family h)
  isGaussian : ∀ h, IsGaussian (family h)
  mean_eq (h u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) :
    (∫ x, ⟪u, x⟫ ∂(family h)) = ⟪u, h⟫
  cov_eq (h u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) :
    (∫ x, ⟪u, x - h⟫ * ⟪v, x - h⟫ ∂(family h)) =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (cov.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫
formalizationNotes: Packaged as a Prop predicate on a measure family with separate fields for Gaussianity, mean, and covariance (stated via inner-product integrals) because Mathlib lacks a direct multivariateGaussian primitive at this commit. The closed-form log-likelihood ratio is recorded separately as HasGaussianShiftLogLikelihoodRatio.

hypotheses.label: positive definite covariance
hypotheses.note: The covariance matrix Σ is positive definite, so the shift experiment is nondegenerate.

hypotheses.label: Gaussian members
hypotheses.note: Each member of the family is a Gaussian probability measure.

hypotheses.label: mean equals the shift
hypotheses.note: The member indexed by h has mean h, stated through ∫⟨u, x⟩ = ⟨u, h⟩ for every u.

hypotheses.label: common covariance
hypotheses.note: Every member has the same covariance Σ, stated through the centred bilinear integral.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The Gaussian shift experiment and its affine log-likelihood ratio are the canonical limit object of Le Cam's theory of asymptotic equivalence of experiments. The foundational reference is L. Le Cam, "Locally asymptotically normal families of distributions," *University of California Publications in Statistics* **3** (1960), 37–98; see also L. Le Cam, *Asymptotic Methods in Statistical Decision Theory*, Springer, 1986. The synthesis follows van der Vaart (1998), Chapter 7.

title: Equivariant-in-Law Estimator
informal: A randomized estimator $T$ of $A\cdot h$ in the Gaussian shift experiment, encoded as a Markov kernel $\mathbb{R}^k\rightsquigarrow\mathbb{R}^d$, is equivariant-in-law if for every $h$, the distribution of $T(X)-A\cdot h$ under $X\sim N(h,S)$ equals one common probability measure $L$ — i.e. the law of $T-Ah$ does not depend on $h$. That common $L$ is the null distribution of $T$.
summary: A randomized estimator (Markov kernel) whose centred law T(X) − Ah under N(h,S) is the same probability measure for every shift h.
leanSignature:
structure IsEquivariantInLaw
    (T : Kernel (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin k) ℝ)
    (S : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) : Prop where
  invariant_law :
    ∃ L : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)),
      IsProbabilityMeasure L ∧
      ∀ h : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k),
        (T ∘ₘ (multivariateGaussian h S)).map
            (fun y => y - (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin d → ℝ)).symm
              (A.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin k → ℝ)) h)))
          = L
formalizationNotes: The estimator is encoded as a Markov kernel; the law of T(X) is T ∘ₘ N(h,S), pushed forward by the translation y ↦ y − Ah. The single field invariant_law Skolemizes the common null distribution L (accessor IsEquivariantInLaw.nullDist). The covariance written Σ in the literature is named S in Lean, since Σ is reserved.

hypotheses.label: shift-invariant centred law
hypotheses.note: One probability measure L equals the law of T(X) − Ah when X is drawn from N(h, S), simultaneously for every shift h.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The notion of an equivariant-in-law (regular) estimator and the resulting convolution structure originate with the convolution theorem of J. Hájek, "A characterization of limiting distributions of regular estimates," *Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und Verwandte Gebiete* **14** (1970), 323–330, with parallel contributions by L. Le Cam and by N. Inagaki, "On the limiting distribution of a sequence of estimators with uniformity property," *Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics* **22** (1970), 1–13. The finite-dimensional Gaussian-shift formulation used here is the standard distillation (vdV §8.4).

title: Parametric Submodel is Differentiable in Quadratic Mean
informal: The finite-dimensional parametric submodel constructed from a bounded family of mixture scores $g_P$ that are orthonormal in $L^2(P)$ is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta=0$ with multi-dimensional score $g_{P,\text{total}}$: the integrated squared Hellinger residual $\int\big(\sqrt{p_\theta}-1-\tfrac12\langle\theta,g_{P,\text{total}}\rangle\big)^2$ is $o(\|\theta\|^2)$ as $\theta\to0$.
summary: The submodel built from bounded orthonormal mixture scores is differentiable in quadratic mean at zero with score g_P_total.
leanSignature:
theorem paramSubmodel_DQM :
    DifferentiableQuadraticMean (paramSubmodel g_P hg h_orth) P 0 (g_P_total g_P)
formalizationNotes: The score family g_P, its boundedness hg (IsBoundedMixtureScores) and L²(P)-orthonormality h_orth are section variables, not explicit binders in the signature line. DQM is proven at θ = 0 for the SubmodelFromScores construction. The rate follows from the Taylor inequality |√(1+u)−1−u/2| ≤ u²/2 for 0 ≤ 1+u together with the uniform bound on the perturbation, giving an O(‖θ‖⁴) integrated squared residual, hence o(‖θ‖²).

hypotheses.label: bounded score directions
hypotheses.note: The submodel is the mixture family built from the uniformly bounded score directions g_P.

hypotheses.label: orthonormal scores
hypotheses.note: The score directions are orthonormal in L²(P), which makes the Fisher information of the submodel the identity.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.

title: Local Asymptotic Normality Expansion
informal: Let $(P_\theta)$ be a parametric family that is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$, with $p_\theta$ a genuine $\mu$-density for every $\theta$ (nonnegative, integrable, integrating to $1$), and let $X_i$ be i.i.d. with law $P_{\theta_0}$. Then for any $h_n\to h$ the score has zero mean, the Fisher information $\langle h,I_{\theta_0}h\rangle$ is finite in every direction, and the log-likelihood ratio admits the expansion $$\log\prod_{i\le n}\frac{p_{\theta_0+h_n/\sqrt n}(X_i)}{p_{\theta_0}(X_i)}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i\le n}\langle h,\ell(X_i)\rangle-\tfrac12\langle h,I_{\theta_0}h\rangle+o_P(1).$$
summary: Under DQM at theta0 with iid data and a converging local parameter sequence, the log-likelihood ratio of local alternatives expands as a score average minus half the Fisher quadratic form plus o_P(1).
leanSignature:
theorem LAN_expansion
    {k : ℕ}
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))) (μ : Measure 𝓧)
    [SigmaFinite μ]
    (θ₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
    (ℓ : 𝓧 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (hPDF : IsPDFOf M μ)
    (hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (h : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) (h_n : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
    (hconv : Filter.Tendsto h_n Filter.atTop (𝓝 h))
    (X : ℕ → Ω → 𝓧) (hX_meas : ∀ i, Measurable (X i))
    (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (X i) (X j) P)
    (hident : ∀ i, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) P P)
    (hlaw : Measure.map (X 0) P
              = μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (M.density θ₀ x)) :
    (∀ u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), ∫ x, ⟪u, ℓ x⟫ * M.density θ₀ x ∂μ = 0) ∧
    (∀ u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k),
      Integrable (fun x => ⟪u, ℓ x⟫ ^ 2 * M.density θ₀ x) μ) ∧
    TendstoInMeasure P
      (fun n ω =>
        (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n,
          Real.log (M.density (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h_n n) (X i ω)
                    / M.density θ₀ (X i ω)))
        - (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, ⟪h, ℓ (X i ω)⟫
        + (1/2 : ℝ) * fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ h h)
      Filter.atTop (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))
formalizationNotes: The o_P(1) remainder is encoded as TendstoInMeasure to 0. The conclusion bundles three claims: score mean zero (i), finite Fisher information (ii), and the LAN expansion (iii). hPDF (IsPDFOf) packages that p_θ normalises and is integrable for every θ — the tacit assumption in writing p_θ. The iid sample is given by explicit pairwise-independence, identical-distribution, and law fields.

hypotheses.note: Each p_θ is a nonnegative integrable μ-density integrating to 1.

hypotheses.label: differentiability in quadratic mean
hypotheses.note: The family is differentiable in quadratic mean at θ₀ with score ℓ.

hypotheses.label: converging local parameter
hypotheses.note: The local parameter sequence h_n converges to h.

hypotheses.label: i.i.d. sample at the truth
hypotheses.note: The observations are independent, identically distributed, with law P at θ₀.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: Local asymptotic normality originates with L. Le Cam, "Locally asymptotically normal families of distributions," *University of California Publications in Statistics* **3** (1960), 37–98, where the LAN concept and the quadratic log-likelihood expansion were introduced. The differentiability-in-quadratic-mean formulation under which Theorem 7.2 is stated is the modern presentation (Le Cam and Hájek) adopted by van der Vaart.

title: Contiguity of Local Alternatives
informal: Suppose the family is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$ and has nonsingular Fisher information $J$, and that the log-likelihood ratio of the local alternative converges weakly under $P^n_{\theta_0}$ to $N(-v/2,\,v)$, where $v=\langle h,Jh\rangle$, where $P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}$ is $P^n_{\theta_0}$ reweighted by the exponential of that log-likelihood ratio. Then, by Le Cam’s first lemma, the sequences $P^n_{\theta_0}$ and $P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}$ are mutually contiguous: a sequence of events is asymptotically negligible under one exactly when it is asymptotically negligible under the other.
summary: Under DQM and asymptotic log-normality of the local likelihood ratio, the local alternatives and the base product measures are mutually contiguous (Le Cam's first lemma).
leanSignature:
theorem contiguous_local_alternatives
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧) [SigmaFinite μ]
    [∀ θ : Θ k, ∀ n, IsProbabilityMeasure (productMeasure M μ θ n)]
    (θ₀ : Θ k) (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ k) (_hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (_hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (J : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) (_hJ_pd : Matrix.PosDef J)
    (_hJ : ∀ u v : Θ k, fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ u v =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (J.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫)
    (h : Θ k)
    (hL_meas : ∀ n : ℕ, Measurable (logLikelihood M θ₀ h n))
    (hL_is_log_ratio : ∀ n : ℕ,
        productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n =
          (productMeasure M μ θ₀ n).withDensity
            (fun ω => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (logLikelihood M θ₀ h n ω))))
    (v : NNReal)
    (h_log_weak :
      WeakConverges (fun n => (productMeasure M μ θ₀ n).map (logLikelihood M θ₀ h n))
        (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal (-(v : ℝ) / 2) v)) :
    Contiguity.MutuallyContiguous (ι := ℕ)
      (Ω := fun n => Fin n → 𝓧) atTop
      (fun n => productMeasure M μ θ₀ n)
      (fun n => productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n)
formalizationNotes: The asymptotic log-normality of the likelihood ratio (the consequence of DQM) is the operative input. The DQM and Fisher hypotheses (_hDQM, _hJ_pd, _hJ) are carried but the proof reduces to the abstract Le Cam first lemma packaged as mutuallyContiguous_of_asymptotically_log_normal, fed the operative inputs hL_is_log_ratio (change of measure) and h_log_weak (weak convergence of the log-ratio to N(-v/2, v)).

hypotheses.label: differentiability in quadratic mean
hypotheses.note: The family is differentiable in quadratic mean at θ₀ with score ℓ.

hypotheses.label: nonsingular Fisher information
hypotheses.note: The Fisher information matrix J is positive definite.

hypotheses.label: log-normal limit of the likelihood ratio
hypotheses.note: Under the base product measure, the local log-likelihood ratio converges weakly to the Gaussian law with mean −v/2 and variance v.

hypotheses.label: exponential change of measure
hypotheses.note: The local alternative is the base product measure reweighted by the exponential of the log-likelihood ratio.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.

title: Regularity Supplies the (8.2) Weak-Convergence Input
informal: A regular estimator sequence $T_n$ for $\psi(\theta)$ at $\theta_0$ — one for which $\sqrt n\,(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n))$ has, under each local alternative $P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}$, one and the same weak limit $L_\theta$ supplies precisely the weak-convergence input required by the asymptotic representation theorem and the convolution lower bound: for every $h$, $$\sqrt n\,\bigl(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n)\bigr)\xrightarrow{P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}} L_\theta,$$ the family of limit laws being the constant family $h\mapsto L_\theta$.
summary: A regular estimator sequence yields, for every h, weak convergence of the rescaled recentred statistic to the constant limit law required by the convolution-theorem lower bound.
leanSignature:
theorem regularity_implies_8_2_hypothesis
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧)
    (θ₀ : Θ k)
    (ψ : Θ k → 𝓨 d)
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → 𝓨 d)
    (hReg : RegularEstimatorSequence M μ θ₀ ψ T) :
    ∀ h : Θ k,
      WeakConverges
        (fun n : ℕ =>
          (productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n).map
            (fun x => (Real.sqrt n) •
              (T n x - ψ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h))))
        hReg.limitDist
formalizationNotes: A local-glue lemma feeding the §8.2 lower-bound input: it unfolds RegularEstimatorSequence.tendsto, choosing the h-indexed limit family as the constant family fun _ => hReg.limitDist. The proof body is exactly hReg.tendsto.

hypotheses.label: regular estimator sequence
hypotheses.note: The rescaled estimator recentred at the perturbed truth converges weakly, under every local alternative, to one and the same limit law.

reference.formal: A. W. van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Cambridge Series in Statistical and Probabilistic Mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 1998.
reference.biblio: The convolution theorem originates with J. Hájek, "A characterization of limiting distributions of regular estimates," *Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete* **14** (1970), 323–330: the limiting law of any regular estimator in a locally asymptotically normal family is a convolution of the optimal Gaussian with a residual measure. An essentially equivalent result was obtained independently by N. Inagaki, *Annals of the Institute of Statistical Mathematics* **22** (1970), 1–13. The underlying local-asymptotic framework and an early lower bound are due to L. Le Cam, "On some asymptotic properties of maximum likelihood estimates and related Bayes' estimates," *University of California Publications in Statistics* **1** (1953), 277–330 (hence "Hájek–Le Cam"); vdV Theorem 8.8 is the synthesis.

title: Asymptotic Representation Theorem (LAN)
informal: Assume the family is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$, with nonsingular Fisher information $J$ and $p_\theta$ a genuine $\mu$-density for every $\theta$, and that a statistic sequence $T_n$ converges weakly to a law $L_h$ under each local alternative $P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}$. Then there exists a single Markov kernel $\kappa$ from $\mathbb R^k$ to the sample space of $T_n$ such that, for every $h$, $$L_h(B)=\int\kappa(z,B)\,dN\bigl(h,J^{-1}\bigr)(z);$$ that is, every limit law is obtained by drawing $Z\sim N(h,J^{-1})$ in the Gaussian shift experiment and then randomizing through one fixed kernel. Nothing the statistic can do in the limit exceeds what the Gaussian shift experiment allows.
summary: Under DQM with non-singular Fisher information, any weakly converging statistic sequence's limit laws factor as N(h, J-inverse) bound through a single Markov kernel.
leanSignature:
theorem LAN_representation_vdV
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧) [SigmaFinite μ]
    (θ₀ : Θ k) (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ k) (hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (J : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) (hJ_pd : Matrix.PosDef J)
    (hJ : ∀ u v : Θ k, fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ u v =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (J.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫)
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → 𝓨 d) (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T n))
    (L : Θ k → Measure (𝓨 d)) [∀ h, IsProbabilityMeasure (L h)]
    (hT_weak : ∀ h : Θ k,
      WeakConverges
        (fun n => (productMeasure M μ (θ₀ + (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ • h) n).map (T n)) (L h))
    [StandardBorelSpace (𝓨 d)] [Nonempty (𝓨 d)]
    [HasOuterApproxClosed (𝓨 d)] [BorelSpace (𝓨 d)]
    (hPDF : IsPDFOf M μ) :
    ∃ κ : Kernel (Θ k) (𝓨 d), IsMarkovKernel κ ∧
      ∀ h : Θ k, L h = (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian h J⁻¹).bind κ
formalizationNotes: This is the asymptotic-representation form: matching estimators in the LAN sequence to the Gaussian limit experiment. LAN_representation_vdV is a thin compatibility alias delegating to LAN_representation; the paper-literal name is LAN_representation. Standard-Borel / Borel / outer-approximation instances on the value space are encoding requirements for the kernel disintegration. The LAN/Le Cam transfer routes through DQM-derived singular-mass control, so no common-support hypothesis is needed.

title: Anderson's Lemma (Set Form)
informal: Let $ u = N(0, S)$ be a centered multivariate Gaussian with positive-semidefinite covariance $S$, and let $C$ be a measurable, convex, symmetric set. Then for every shift $y$, $$ u(C-y)\le u(C).$$
summary: For a centered Gaussian with positive-semidefinite covariance, any translate of a convex symmetric measurable set has Gaussian measure at most that of the centred set.
leanSignature:
theorem anderson_lemma_set
    {S : Matrix ι ι ℝ} (hS : S.PosSemidef)
    {C : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)} (hC_meas : MeasurableSet C)
    (hC_conv : Convex ℝ C) (hC_symm : ∀ x ∈ C, -x ∈ C)
    (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) :
    (multivariateGaussian 0 S) {x | x + y ∈ C} ≤ (multivariateGaussian 0 S) C
formalizationNotes: Allows S merely positive-semidefinite (not only positive-definite), matching the canonical statement; proven by cases including S = 0 (Dirac), S positive-definite, and the singular-PSD degenerate branch. The shifted set is spelled {x | x + y ∈ C} = C − y. The centred set has the largest Gaussian measure among all its translates.

hypotheses.note: The covariance matrix S is positive semidefinite, so degenerate Gaussians are allowed.

title: Hájek–Le Cam Convolution Theorem
informal: Suppose the experiment is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$ and has nonsingular Fisher information $J$, the target functional $\psi$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ with derivative $\dot\psi$, and $T_n$ is a regular estimator sequence for $\psi(\theta)$, i.e. $\sqrt n(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n))$ converges weakly to one $h$-independent law $L_\theta$ under every local alternative. Then there is a probability measure $M_\theta$ with $$L_\theta=N\bigl(0,\ \dot\psi\,J^{-1}\,\dot\psi^{\mathsf T}\bigr)*M_\theta,$$ so the limit law of any regular estimator is the optimal Gaussian law convolved with extra noise; the Gaussian alone is the best attainable limit.
summary: The limit law of any regular estimator of psi factors as the convolution of the optimal Gaussian N(0, psidot J-inverse psidot-transpose) with some probability measure.
leanSignature:
theorem hajek_le_cam_convolution_theorem
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧) [SigmaFinite μ]
    (θ₀ : Θ k) (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ k) (hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (J : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) (hJ_pd : Matrix.PosDef J)
    (hJ_fisher : ∀ u v : Θ k, fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ u v =
      ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (J.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫)
    (ψ : Θ k → 𝓨 d) (ψDot : Θ k →L[ℝ] 𝓨 d)
    (hψ_diff : HasFDerivAt ψ ψDot θ₀)
    (ψDotMat : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin k) ℝ)
    (h_ψDot_mat : ∀ h : Θ k,
      ψDot h = (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (ψDotMat.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) h)))
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → 𝓨 d) (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T n))
    (hReg : RegularEstimatorSequence M μ θ₀ ψ T)
    (hPDF : IsPDFOf M μ) :
    ∃ M_θ : Measure (𝓨 d),
      IsProbabilityMeasure M_θ ∧
      hReg.limitDist =
        (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : 𝓨 d)
          (ψDotMat * J⁻¹ * ψDotMat.transpose)) ∗ M_θ

title: Local Asymptotic Minimax Bound
informal: Suppose the family is differentiable in quadratic mean at $\theta_0$ with score $\ell$ and has nonsingular Fisher information $J$, the functional $\psi$ is Fréchet differentiable at $\theta_0$ with derivative $\dot\psi$, the loss $L$ is lower semicontinuous and bowl-shaped — measurable, symmetric about the origin, with convex sublevel sets, and $\sqrt n\,(T_n-\psi(\theta_0))$ is uniformly tight under $P^n_{\theta_0}$. Then $$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\ \mathbb E_{P^n_{\theta_0+h/\sqrt n}}\Bigl[L\bigl(\sqrt n\,(T_n-\psi(\theta_0+h/\sqrt n))\bigr)\Bigr]\ \ge\ \int L\,dN\bigl(0,\ \dot\psi\,J^{-1}\,\dot\psi^{\mathsf T}\bigr).$$ No estimator can asymptotically beat the risk of the optimal Gaussian experiment.
summary: Under DQM, non-singular Fisher information, a differentiable functional, a bowl-shaped lsc loss, and tightness, the local asymptotic minimax risk is at least the optimal Gaussian risk.
leanSignature:
theorem local_asymptotic_minimax_bound
    (M : ParametricFamily 𝓧 (Θ k)) (μ : Measure 𝓧) [SigmaFinite μ]
    (θ₀ : Θ k) (ℓ : 𝓧 → Θ k)
    (hℓ : Measurable ℓ)
    (hDQM : DifferentiableQuadraticMean M μ θ₀ ℓ)
    (J : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ) (hJ : J.PosDef)
    (hJ_fisher : ∀ u v : Θ k, fisherInformation M μ θ₀ ℓ u v
      = ⟪u, (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (J.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) v))⟫)
    (ψ : Θ k → 𝓨 d)
    (ψDot : Θ k →L[ℝ] 𝓨 d)
    (hψ_diff : HasFDerivAt ψ ψDot θ₀)
    (ψDotMat : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin k) ℝ)
    (h_ψDot_mat : ∀ h : Θ k,
      ψDot h = (WithLp.equiv 2 _).symm (ψDotMat.mulVec ((WithLp.equiv 2 _) h)))
    (T : ∀ n, (Fin n → 𝓧) → 𝓨 d) (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T n))
    (L : 𝓨 d → ℝ≥0∞)
    (hL_bowl : BowlShaped L)
    (hL_lsc : LowerSemicontinuous L)
    (hTight : MeasureTheory.IsTightMeasureSet
        (Set.range (fun n : ℕ =>
          (AsymptoticRepresentation.productMeasure M μ θ₀ n).map
            (fun ω => (Real.sqrt n) • (T n ω - ψ θ₀)))))
    (hPDF : IsPDFOf M μ) :
    localAsymptoticRisk M μ θ₀ T ψ L
      ≥ ∫⁻ y, L y ∂(multivariateGaussian (0 : 𝓨 d)
                    (ψDotMat * J⁻¹ * ψDotMat.transpose))

title: Tangent set / tangent space
informal: At a probability measure $P$, a tangent set is a collection of mean-zero square-integrable functions in $L^2_0(P)$, each of which is the score of a submodel through $P$. Formally it consists of a set of admissible score directions inside $L^2_0(P)$ together with, for every direction $g$ in that set, a quadratic-mean-differentiable curve $t\mapsto Q_t$ with $Q_0=P$ whose score is exactly $g$. The closed linear span of a tangent set is the tangent space; it plays the role of the parameter space of the local Gaussian experiment.
summary: A tangent set is a set of QMD-realizable score directions in L²₀(P); its closed linear span is the tangent space.
leanSignature:
structure TangentSpec (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] where
  carrier : Set ↥(L2ZeroMean P)
  submodelOf : ∀ g ∈ carrier, ∃ γ : AsymptoticStatistics.Core.QMDPath.QMDPath P,
    γ.score = g
formalizationNotes: Separates the tangent set (this structure) from the tangent space (the derived `tangentSpace` closed-linear-span submodule). The realizing-path obligation `submodelOf` is carrier-scoped, matching the definition that each carrier element is a genuine QMD score; the L²-closure may contain limit points with no realizing path. Closure under scaling or addition is a regularity property, not part of the definition (one works with one-sided tangent cones), so it is not imposed here. The associated tangent space is the derived closed linear span of the tangent set.

title: Regular estimator (semiparametric)
informal: Let $\psi$ be a scalar functional of the underlying law, differentiable along the tangent space at $P$ with derivative $d\psi$, and let $\tilde\psi_P$ be an efficient influence function for $d\psi$, i.e. an element of the tangent space with $d\psi(g)=\langle\tilde\psi_P,g\rangle$ for every tangent direction $g$. A sequence $T_n$ of estimators is regular at $P$ relative to the tangent set with limit law $L$ if, for every direction $g$ in the linear span of the tangent set and every quadratic-mean-differentiable curve through $P$ whose score is $g$, the rescaled estimator recentred at the perturbed truth has the same weak limit: $$\sqrt n\,\bigl(T_n-\psi(P_{1/\sqrt n,\,g})\bigr)\rightsquigarrow L\qquad\text{under }P^n_{1/\sqrt n,\,g},$$ with $L$ not depending on $g$. This shift-invariance is what rules out estimators that are superefficient at $P$ at the cost of erratic behaviour nearby.
summary: An estimator is regular if the perturbed-truth-recentered rescaled statistic has the same weak limit L along every QMD score direction.
leanSignature:
def IsRegularEstimator
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (T_set : TangentSpec P)
    (ψ : Measure Ω → ℝ)
    {IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)}
    (hψ : PathwiseDifferentiableAt P (tangentSpace T_set) ψ)
    (_hEIF : IsEfficientInfluenceFunction P (tangentSpace T_set)
              hψ.derivative IF_eff)
    (T_n : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → ℝ)
    (L : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure L] : Prop :=
  ∀ (g : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))
    (_hg : (g : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ T_set.carrier)
    (curve : QMDPath P)
    (_hscore : curve.score = g),
    WeakConverges
      (fun n : ℕ =>
        (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi
            (fun _ : Fin n => curve.curve ((Real.sqrt n)⁻¹))).map
          (fun X : Fin n → Ω =>
            Real.sqrt n *
              (T_n n X - ψ (curve.curve ((Real.sqrt n)⁻¹)))))
      L
formalizationNotes: Stated in the canonical recenter-at-perturbed-truth convention so the limit `L` is direction-independent. `hEIF` and `hψ` carry no proof obligation in the definition itself; they are present so the derived Hájek-shift form (`hajek_shift_form`) can be expressed in the same predicate's data — the equivalent Hájek-shift form recenters at $\psi(P)$ with deterministic shift $\langle \tilde{\psi}_P, g\rangle$. Quantification is over the algebraic span `Submodule.span ℝ T_set.carrier`.

title: Coarsening at random
informal: A coarsening map $M:\Omega_{\mathrm{full}}\to\Omega_{\mathrm{obs}}$ is at random under the full-data law $P_{\mathrm{full}}$ if $P_{\mathrm{full}}$ is recovered by first drawing an observed value $y$ from the induced law $P_{\mathrm{obs}}=P_{\mathrm{full}}\circ M^{-1}$ and then drawing the full datum from a Markov kernel $\kappa(y,\cdot)$, where $\kappa(y,\cdot)$ is concentrated on the fibre $\{x:M(x)=y\}$ for $P_{\mathrm{obs}}$-almost every $y$. The kernel is then a version of the conditional law of the full data given what was observed, and it redistributes mass only within a fibre — the coarsening mechanism carries no further information about the full data.
summary: Coarsening at random: the full law disintegrates over the observed law via a fibre-concentrated kernel.
leanSignature:
def IsCoarseningAtRandom
    (M : Ω_full → Ω_obs) (P_full : Measure Ω_full) : Prop :=
  ∃ κ : Kernel Ω_obs Ω_full,
    P_full = (P_full.map M).bind κ ∧
    ∀ᵐ y ∂(P_full.map M), ∀ᵐ x ∂(κ y), M x = y
formalizationNotes: Stated in the kernel-disintegration form: existence of a `ProbabilityTheory.Kernel` disintegrating `P_full` over `P_full.map M`, plus the regularity clause that the kernel concentrates on the M-fibre. For deterministic coarsenings on standard Borel spaces this is essentially automatic via Mathlib's `condDistrib`; the substantive content appears at the family level. Coarsening at random is a genuine restriction: outcome-dependent missingness is in general not at random, so theorems requiring it list it as an explicit hypothesis.

hypotheses.label: disintegration through a kernel
hypotheses.note: The full law is obtained by drawing the observed value from its own law and then the full datum from a Markov kernel.

title: QMD score has mean zero and is square-integrable
informal: The score of a quadratic-mean-differentiable submodel is mean-zero and square-integrable. If a measurable function $g$ satisfies the QMD limit on the square-root density expansion $\bigl\| \sqrt{p_t} - \sqrt{p_0} - \tfrac{t}{2}\, g\,\sqrt{p_0}\bigr\|_{L^2(\mu)} = o(t)$ along a family of probability measures through $P$ and dominated by $\mu$, then $g$ agrees $P$-a.e. with an element of $L^2_0(P)$.
summary: A function satisfying the QMD square-root-density limit is P-a.e. equal to a mean-zero, square-integrable function.
leanSignature:
theorem score_in_L2ZeroMean
    {P : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    {μ : Measure Ω} [SigmaFinite μ] (curve : ℝ → Measure Ω)
    (h_prob : ∀ t, IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t))
    (h_zero : curve 0 = P) (h_ac : ∀ t, curve t ≪ μ)
    (g : Ω → ℝ) (hg_meas : Measurable g)
    (h_qmd :
      Tendsto
        (fun t : ℝ =>
          eLpNorm (fun ω : Ω =>
            Real.sqrt ((curve t).rnDeriv μ ω).toReal
              - Real.sqrt ((curve 0).rnDeriv μ ω).toReal
              - (t / 2) * g ω
                  * Real.sqrt ((curve 0).rnDeriv μ ω).toReal)
            2 μ / ENNReal.ofReal |t|)
        (𝓝[≠] 0) (𝓝 (0 : ℝ≥0∞))) :
    ∃ g' : ↥(L2ZeroMean P), g =ᵐ[P] (g' : Ω → ℝ)
formalizationNotes: Dominated specialisation (fixed σ-finite μ, densities pt = dQt/dμ). The QMD condition is stated in ℝ≥0∞-quotient form `eLpNorm … / ENNReal.ofReal |t| → 0`, which genuinely forces square-integrability of the residual (a `.toReal²/t²` form would be vacuously satisfied when the residual leaves L²). The `IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t)` hypothesis is added — needed for the L²(μ)-norm bound on √(rnDeriv). This is the analytic part of Lemma 25.14. In particular, this means $\int g\,dP = 0$ and $g \in L^2(P)$.

title: EIF as orthogonal projection of an influence function
informal: For any influence function $\mathrm{IF}$ of a pathwise derivative $d\psi : T \to_L \mathbb{R}$ (not necessarily lying in the tangent space $T$), the orthogonal projection of $\mathrm{IF}$ onto $T$ is the efficient influence function for $d\psi$. Concretely, $\tilde\psi_P = \Pi_T \mathrm{IF}$ both represents $d\psi$ on $T$ and lies in $T$: the residual $\mathrm{IF} - \Pi_T \mathrm{IF} \in T^\perp$, so $\langle \Pi_T \mathrm{IF}, g\rangle = \langle \mathrm{IF}, g\rangle = d\psi(g)$ for every $g \in T$.
summary: Projecting any influence function onto the tangent space yields the efficient influence function.

formalizationNotes: The `[T.HasOrthogonalProjection]` instance is the standard Hilbert-space side condition for orthogonal projection, automatic when T is closed in a complete inner-product space.

title: Operational efficiency bound (sup-ratio form)
informal: The supremum over the tangent space of the squared inner-product ratio equals the squared norm of the efficient influence function, $$\sup_{g \in T} \frac{\langle \tilde\psi_P, g\rangle^2}{\|g\|^2} = \|\tilde\psi_P\|^2.$$ The upper bound is Cauchy–Schwarz term-by-term; equality is attained at $g = \tilde\psi_P$, which lies in the tangent set $T$.

title: Semiparametric convolution theorem (scalar)
informal: Let $\psi$ be a real functional differentiable along the tangent space at $P$, with efficient influence function $\tilde\psi_P$ — the element of the tangent space representing the derivative, $d\psi(g)=\langle\tilde\psi_P,g\rangle$, and let $T_n$ be a regular estimator sequence for $\psi$ with limit law $L$, i.e. $\sqrt n(T_n-\psi(P_{1/\sqrt n,g}))\rightsquigarrow L$ along every tangent direction $g$. Then: (a) if $L$ has a finite second moment, its variance is bounded below by the efficiency bound, $\|\tilde\psi_P\|^2\le\operatorname{Var}(L)$; and (b) if the tangent set is moreover a convex cone, then $L$ factors as a convolution $L=N\bigl(0,\|\tilde\psi_P\|^2\bigr)*M$ for some probability measure $M$.
summary: For a regular estimator, the asymptotic variance is at least ‖ψ̃‖² and (over a convex cone) the limit law is N(0,‖ψ̃‖²) convolved with a residual.

theorem semiparametric_convolution_theorem

    {ψ : Measure Ω → ℝ}
    (hψ : PathwiseDifferentiableAt P (tangentSpace T_set) ψ)
    {IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P)}
    (hEIF : IsEfficientInfluenceFunction P (tangentSpace T_set)
              hψ.derivative IF_eff)
    (T_n : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → ℝ)
    (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T_n n))
    (L : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure L]
    (hReg : AsymptoticStatistics.LowerBounds.RegularEstimator.IsRegularEstimator
              P T_set ψ hψ hEIF T_n L)
    (hL_memLp : MeasureTheory.MemLp (id : ℝ → ℝ) 2 L) :
    ‖(IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))‖ ^ 2 ≤ (∫ x, (x - ∫ y, y ∂L)^2 ∂L) ∧
    ((∀ x ∈ T_set.carrier, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t • x ∈ T_set.carrier) →
     (∀ x ∈ T_set.carrier, ∀ y ∈ T_set.carrier,
        ∀ a b : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 →
        a • x + b • y ∈ T_set.carrier) →
     let sigma_sq : ℝ≥0 :=
       ⟨‖(IF_eff : ↥(L2ZeroMean P))‖ ^ 2, sq_nonneg _⟩
     ∃ M : Measure ℝ, IsProbabilityMeasure M ∧
       L = MeasureTheory.Measure.conv
              (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 sigma_sq) M)

Probab.* **1** (1972), 245–261, recast and generalized it (see also Inagaki, *Ann. Inst. Statist. Math.* **22** (1970), 1–13). The semiparametric formulation follows van der Vaart's Theorem 25.20.

title: Semiparametric convolution theorem (vector)
informal: The vector-valued convolution theorem for a $\mathbb{R}^k$-valued functional $\psi$ with efficient influence function tuple $(\tilde\psi_{P,1},\dots,\tilde\psi_{P,k})$ and a regular vector estimator with limit law $L$. (a) When $L$ has finite second moments, the asymptotic covariance matrix $\Sigma$ minus the Gram matrix $G = P\,\tilde\psi_P\tilde\psi_P^\top$ is positive semidefinite, $\Sigma - G \succeq 0$. (b) The limit law decomposes as $L = N(0, G) * M$ for some probability measure $M$.
summary: Vector form: Σ − G is PSD and L = N(0,G) * M, where G is the Gram matrix of the EIF tuple.
leanSignature:
theorem semiparametric_convolution_theorem_vec
    {ψ : Measure Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)}
    (hψ : PathwiseDifferentiableAt_vec P (tangentSpace T_set) ψ)
    {IF_eff : Fin k → ↥(L2ZeroMean P)}
    (hEIF : IsEfficientInfluenceFunction_vec hψ.derivative IF_eff)
    (T_n : ∀ n, (Fin n → Ω) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))
    (hT_meas : ∀ n, Measurable (T_n n))
    (L : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))) [IsProbabilityMeasure L]
    (hReg : IsRegularEstimator_vec P T_set ψ hψ hEIF T_n L)
    (hL_memLp : MemLp (id : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) → _) 2 L) :
    let G : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ := Matrix.gram ℝ IF_eff
    let Sigma : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ := fun i j =>
      ∫ y, (y.ofLp i - ∫ z, z.ofLp i ∂L)
          * (y.ofLp j - ∫ z, z.ofLp j ∂L) ∂L
    (Sigma - G).PosSemidef ∧
    (∃ M : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)), IsProbabilityMeasure M ∧
      L = (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k)) G) ∗ M)
formalizationNotes: Combined (a) ∧ (b) package delegating to the vec per-clause theorems. The covariance bound is the Loewner-order matrix form `Σ - G PosSemidef`; the covariance `P ψ̃ ψ̃ᵀ` is the Gram matrix `Matrix.gram ℝ IF_eff`. Clause (a) is proved by Cramér–Wold per-direction-λ reduction to the scalar clause.

title: Local asymptotic minimax (vector)
informal: Assume the tangent set is closed under nonnegative scaling, under convex combinations and under negation — together these make it a linear subspace of $L^2_0(P)$ — and let the loss be nonnegative and bowl-shaped: measurable, symmetric about the origin, with convex sublevel sets. Then the local asymptotic minimax risk of any estimator sequence is bounded below by the Gaussian risk: $$\sup_{I}\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{g\in I}\ \mathbb E_{P_{1/\sqrt n,g}}\ \ell\bigl(\sqrt n(T_n-\psi(P_{1/\sqrt n,g}))\bigr)\ \ge\ \int \ell\,dN\bigl(0,\ P\tilde\psi_P\tilde\psi_P^{\mathsf T}\bigr),$$ where the outer supremum runs over finite subsets $I$ of the tangent set and the Gaussian covariance is the Gram matrix of the efficient influence functions. No estimator beats the Gaussian shift limit.
summary: Over a convex-cone tangent, the local minimax risk for a subconvex loss is at least its integral against N(0, Gram(ψ̃)).

    (hTight : MeasureTheory.IsTightMeasureSet

            (fun ω => (Real.sqrt n) •

    ⨆ I : { S : Finset ↥(L2ZeroMean P) //
